question: In March 2025, Operation Brahma was launched to assist earthquake hit _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Myanmar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Operation Brahma (ऑपरेशन ब्रह्मा) was launched by India in March 2025 to provide humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) to Myanmar after a devastating earthquake.

• A powerful earthquake of magnitude around 7.7 struck central Myanmar near Mandalay/Sagaing on 28 March 2025, causing widespread destruction.

• India rushed relief material, field hospital teams, search-and-rescue personnel (NDRF) and medical supplies as a 'first responder'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India frequently names its relief missions distinctly, e.g. Operation Dost (Turkey-Syria earthquake, 2023).

• India's HADR outreach reflects its 'Neighbourhood First' and 'Act East' policies.

• The Indian Air Force and Navy transported aid to Myanmar under this operation.

NOTE

• Bangladesh (Option 1): India's eastern neighbour; not the country assisted under Operation Brahma.

• Nepal (Option 3): Himalayan neighbour struck by a major quake in 2015 (Operation Maitri), not 2025.

• Turkey (Option 4): Assisted earlier under Operation Dost after the 2023 earthquake, not Operation Brahma.

question: Srinivasa Ramanujan, the mathematical genius, was passed away on April 26, 1920, at about what age?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 32.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Srinivasa Ramanujan (श्रीनिवास रामानुजन) was born on 22 December 1887 and died on 26 April 1920, making him about 32 years old at death.

• He was a self-taught genius who made extraordinary contributions to number theory, infinite series, continued fractions and mathematical analysis.

• His birthday, 22 December, is celebrated as National Mathematics Day in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He collaborated with British mathematician G. H. Hardy at Cambridge and became a Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS).

• The number 1729 is famous as the 'Hardy–Ramanujan number' (taxicab number).

• His life was depicted in the film 'The Man Who Knew Infinity'.

NOTE

• 21 (Option 1): Too young; he was already in England by this age doing advanced research.

• 47 (Option 3): Incorrect; he died tragically young at 32, not 47.

• 58 (Option 4): Incorrect; Ramanujan did not live anywhere near this age.

question: Who became the Chairman of ISRO in January 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is V. Narayanan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• V. Narayanan (वी. नारायणन) took over as the Chairman of ISRO and Secretary, Department of Space, in January 2025.

• He succeeded S. Somanath and is a distinguished rocket and spacecraft propulsion expert.

• Before this, he headed the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC) of ISRO.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation) was founded in 1969 and is headquartered in Bengaluru.

• Its founder and first chairman was Dr. Vikram Sarabhai.

• V. Narayanan contributed significantly to cryogenic engine development for GSLV missions.

NOTE

• S. Somanath (Option 1): The immediate predecessor who oversaw Chandrayaan-3's success; retired in January 2025.

• K. Sivan (Option 2): ISRO Chairman from 2018 to 2022, associated with Chandrayaan-2.

• Koppillil Radhakrishnan (Option 4): ISRO Chairman from 2009 to 2014, led the Mangalyaan (Mars) mission.

question: In November 2024, who has been appointed as Chief of BrahMos Aerospace?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaiteerth Raghavendra Joshi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Jaiteerth Raghavendra Joshi (जयतीर्थ राघवेंद्र जोशी) was appointed as the CEO and Managing Director (Chief) of BrahMos Aerospace in November 2024.

• He is an eminent missile scientist associated with the DRDO.

• BrahMos Aerospace is an India–Russia joint venture that produces the supersonic BrahMos cruise missile.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The name 'BrahMos' is derived from the rivers Brahmaputra (India) and Moskva (Russia).

• BrahMos is one of the fastest supersonic cruise missiles in the world.

• The joint venture combines DRDO (India) and NPOM (Russia).

NOTE

• Rakesh Sharma (Option 2): The first Indian to travel to space (aboard Soyuz T-11, 1984), not linked to BrahMos.

• Jitender Pal Singh (Option 3): Not the appointed BrahMos chief.

• M. Mohan (Option 4): Not the appointed BrahMos chief.

question: In October 2024, who has been appointed as the Secretary of the Ministry of Coal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vikram Dev Dutt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vikram Dev Dutt (विक्रम देव दत्त) was appointed as the Secretary of the Ministry of Coal in October 2024.

• He is a senior IAS officer who earlier served as Director General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) and CMD of Air India.

• The Ministry of Coal oversees exploration and development of coal and lignite reserves in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India is one of the largest producers and consumers of coal in the world.

• Coal India Limited (CIL) is a Maharatna PSU under the Ministry of Coal.

• Coal is a subject in which reforms like commercial coal mining have been introduced.

NOTE

• Vijender Gupta (Option 2): A BJP politician from Delhi (later Speaker of the Delhi Assembly), not a bureaucrat.

• Rekha Gupta (Option 3): A BJP leader who became Chief Minister of Delhi in 2025, unrelated to the Coal Ministry.

• Gopal Vittal (Option 4): CEO/business executive of Bharti Airtel, not a government secretary.

question: In Budget 2025, the Union Finance Minister announced to set up fifty thousand Atal Tinkering Labs in Government schools in next _____ years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Union Budget 2025-26, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced setting up fifty thousand Atal Tinkering Labs (अटल टिंकरिंग लैब) in Government schools over the next 5 years.

• Atal Tinkering Labs (ATLs) are set up under the Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) to foster creativity, innovation and STEM skills among students.

• They provide young minds hands-on exposure to tools like 3D printers, robotics and electronics kits.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Atal Innovation Mission operates under NITI Aayog.

• ATLs target students of classes 6 to 12.

• The initiative is named after former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

NOTE

• 2 (Option 1): Incorrect timeframe; the announced rollout spans five years.

• 3 (Option 2): Incorrect timeframe stated in Budget 2025.

• 4 (Option 3): Incorrect; the correct period announced was five years.

question: SATAT initiative seen in news in November 2024 is related to which union ministry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• SATAT (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation) is an initiative of the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (पेट्रोलियम और प्राकृतिक गैस मंत्रालय).

• Launched in 2018, it aims to set up Compressed Bio-Gas (CBG) production plants and make CBG available as an automotive fuel.

• It promotes a cleaner, cheaper and self-reliant alternative to conventional fuels.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• SATAT was launched in partnership with Oil Marketing Companies (IOC, BPCL, HPCL).

• Compressed Bio-Gas is produced from waste/biomass sources such as agricultural residue and municipal solid waste.

• It supports India's goals of reducing crude imports and boosting the circular economy.

NOTE

• Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (Option 2): Handles urban housing, smart cities and metro projects; not SATAT.

• Ministry of Urban Development (Option 3): Now merged into Housing & Urban Affairs; not linked to SATAT.

• Ministry of Home Affairs (Option 4): Handles internal security and law and order; unrelated to bio-gas.

question: In Cricket, a _____ will be declared if the umpire thinks the batsman did not have a reasonable opportunity to score off the delivery.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wide Ball.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A Wide Ball (वाइड बॉल) is declared when the ball is bowled so far from the batsman that, in the umpire's judgement, the batsman did not have a reasonable opportunity to score off the delivery.

• A wide adds one run (an extra) to the batting side's total and the delivery is re-bowled (does not count as a legal ball).

• The umpire signals a wide by extending both arms horizontally.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Wides and no-balls are types of 'extras' in cricket.

• In limited-overs cricket, wide-ball rules are stricter, especially down the leg side.

• Byes and leg byes are other categories of extras.

NOTE

• Fast ball (Option 1): A delivery bowled at high pace; not a rule/penalty term.

• Yorker (Option 3): A delivery pitched right at the batsman's feet/base of stumps; a bowling tactic, not an illegal ball.

• Length Ball (Option 4): A delivery pitching at a good length; a normal legal delivery.

question: In Track and Field Events, 800 meters and 1500 meters are of which type of race?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Middle/long.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 800 metres and 1500 metres races are classified as middle-distance (मध्यम दूरी) races in track and field athletics.

• Middle-distance events require a balance of speed and endurance.

• They are run on a standard 400-metre oval track.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sprint events include 100 m, 200 m and 400 m.

• Long-distance track events include 5000 m and 10000 m.

• Track and field falls under the sport of athletics, governed globally by World Athletics.

NOTE

• Sprints (Option 1): Short, very high-speed races such as 100 m and 200 m; not 800/1500 m.

• Hurdles (Option 2): Races involving jumping over barriers (e.g., 110 m hurdles); a different event.

• Road running (Option 4): Events run on roads such as the marathon (42.195 km), not on the track.

question: As of 31 July 2025, who holds the record for most Asian Games medals by an Indian athlete?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PT Usha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• PT Usha (पी.टी. उषा), the legendary sprinter known as the 'Payyoli Express', holds the record for the most Asian Games medals by an Indian athlete, with 11 medals.

• She won her medals across the 1982, 1986, 1990 and 1994 Asian Games.

• She is currently the President of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• She narrowly missed a bronze at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics (400 m hurdles) by 1/100th of a second.

• She has been honoured with the Padma Shri and the Arjuna Award.

• She hails from Payyoli in Kerala.

NOTE

• KD Jadhav (Option 1): Wrestler; India's first individual Olympic medallist (bronze, 1952 Helsinki).

• Sachin Nag (Option 2): Swimmer who won gold at the 1951 Asian Games.

• Dutee Chand (Option 4): Sprinter known for the 100 m; does not hold the most-medals record.

question: In Cricket, a wide ball will add how many run/s to the batting team?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A wide ball (वाइड बॉल) adds one run as an extra to the batting team's total.

• The delivery is not counted as a legal ball and must be re-bowled.

• The umpire signals a wide by stretching both arms out horizontally.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Any additional runs taken by running or from overthrows/boundaries on a wide are added on top of the one wide run.

• Wides come under 'extras' along with no-balls, byes and leg byes.

• A no-ball also adds one run and can bring free-hit rules in limited-overs cricket.

NOTE

• 2 (Option 2): Incorrect; a standard wide adds only one run automatically.

• 3 (Option 3): Incorrect; not the standard penalty for a wide.

• 4 (Option 4): Four runs come from a boundary, not from a wide by rule.

question: As of 31 July 2025, which is the second most successful team in Ranji Trophy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of 31 July 2025, Karnataka (कर्नाटक) is the second most successful team in the Ranji Trophy, having won the title 8 times.

• Mumbai is the most successful team, with a record number of Ranji titles (over 40).

• The Ranji Trophy is India's premier domestic first-class cricket championship.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Ranji Trophy was started in the 1934–35 season.

• It is named after Ranjitsinhji (K. S. Ranjitsinhji), the Jam Sahib of Nawanagar.

• It is organised by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI).

NOTE

• Railways (Option 1): A domestic team that has won the Ranji Trophy twice; not second-most successful.

• Services (Option 2): Represents the armed forces; has not won the Ranji Trophy title.

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Won the Ranji Trophy in the early years but is not the second-most successful.

question: The TrailGuard AI system has implemented as an anti-poaching tool in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Similipal Tiger Reserve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The TrailGuard AI system was implemented as an anti-poaching tool in Similipal Tiger Reserve (सिमलिपाल टाइगर रिजर्व) in Odisha.

• TrailGuard AI uses AI-enabled cameras to detect poachers and intruders in real time and send instant alerts to forest officials.

• Similipal is famous for its rare melanistic (black) tigers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Similipal is located in the Mayurbhanj district of Odisha and is part of a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.

• It is one of the largest tiger reserves in India.

• Technology-based monitoring supports Project Tiger conservation efforts.

NOTE

• Periyar Tiger Reserve (Option 1): Located in Kerala, known for elephants and boat safaris on Periyar Lake.

• Valmiki Tiger Reserve (Option 2): The only tiger reserve in Bihar, in the West Champaran district.

• Gir National Park (Option 4): In Gujarat, the last natural home of the Asiatic lion, not tigers.

question: In August 2025, Assam has launched the Operation Falcon _____.
option_1: to protect one-horned rhinos from poachers
option_2: to deport illegal migrants from Bangladesh to their country
option_3: to tackle naxalism in the state
option_4: to tackle leakages in direct benefit transfer
solution_text:
The correct answer is to protect one-horned rhinos from poachers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In August 2025, Assam launched Operation Falcon (ऑपरेशन फाल्कन) to protect one-horned rhinos from poachers.

• The operation targeted international poaching networks and helped Assam achieve a major reduction (near-zero) in rhino poaching.

• The one-horned rhinoceros is famously found in Kaziranga National Park, Assam.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Indian one-horned rhino (Rhinoceros unicornis) is a Schedule I species under the Wildlife (Protection) Act.

• Kaziranga National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• The IUCN status of the greater one-horned rhino is 'Vulnerable'.

NOTE

• To deport illegal migrants (Option 2): Not the objective of Operation Falcon.

• To tackle naxalism (Option 3): Anti-Naxal operations are separate security initiatives, not this one.

• To tackle leakages in DBT (Option 4): Relates to financial/subsidy governance, not wildlife protection.

question: Table tennis made its Olympic debut in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1988.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Table tennis (टेबल टेनिस) made its Olympic debut at the 1988 Seoul Olympics in South Korea.

• It has been a regular part of the Summer Olympics ever since.

• Events include men's and women's singles, doubles/team and mixed doubles (added in 2021).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Table tennis is governed globally by the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF), founded in 1926.

• China has been the most dominant nation in Olympic table tennis.

• The sport is also popularly known as 'ping pong'.

NOTE

• 1992 (Option 2): The Barcelona Olympics; table tennis was already an Olympic sport by then.

• 1924 (Option 3): The Paris Olympics; table tennis was not yet an Olympic event.

• 1928 (Option 4): The Amsterdam Olympics; table tennis had not debuted at the Games.

question: ICC Men's ODI Cricket World Cup 2027 will be held in which continent?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Africa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ICC Men's ODI Cricket World Cup 2027 will be hosted in Africa (अफ्रीका).

• The co-hosts are South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.

• It will be the 14th edition of the ODI World Cup.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• South Africa previously hosted the 2003 ODI World Cup.

• The ODI World Cup is held every four years, organised by the International Cricket Council (ICC).

• Australia won the 2023 ODI World Cup held in India.

NOTE

• Asia (Option 2): Hosted the 2023 (India) and 2011 (India/Sri Lanka/Bangladesh) editions, not 2027.

• Europe (Option 3): England hosted the 2019 edition, not the 2027 World Cup.

• Australia (Option 4): Hosted the 2015 edition (with New Zealand), not 2027.

question: Which traditional dance of Tamil Nadu is performed by women dancing in a circle while clapping their hands to rhythm?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kummi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kummi (कुम्मी) is a traditional folk dance of Tamil Nadu performed by women who dance in a circle while clapping their hands to keep rhythm.

• It is one of the oldest and simplest folk dances, usually performed without any musical instruments — the clapping provides the beat.

• It is popular during festivals like Pongal and temple celebrations.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Tamil Nadu include Karagattam, Kavadi Attam and Kolattam.

• Bharatanatyam is the famous classical dance of Tamil Nadu.

• Kummi is often performed in a group by women and girls.

NOTE

• Tusu (Option 2): A harvest folk festival/dance associated with West Bengal, Jharkhand and Odisha.

• Giddha (Option 3): A vibrant folk dance performed by women of Punjab.

• Kathi (Option 4): Not a recognised women's circle dance of Tamil Nadu.

question: Interest payment on debt incurred by the government is part of the _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Revenue expenditure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Interest payments on debt incurred by the government are part of Revenue Expenditure (राजस्व व्यय).

• Revenue expenditure is expenditure that neither creates assets nor reduces liabilities.

• Interest payments are one of the largest components of the government's revenue expenditure.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Revenue expenditure is recurring in nature (e.g., salaries, subsidies, pensions, interest payments).

• Capital expenditure creates assets (e.g., building roads, bridges) or reduces liabilities (repaying loan principal).

• The Fiscal Deficit reflects total borrowing requirements, and interest on it forms revenue expenditure.

NOTE

• Revenue receipt (Option 1): Income that neither creates a liability nor reduces assets (e.g., taxes); it is a receipt, not expenditure.

• Capital receipt (Option 3): Receipts that create liabilities (borrowings) or reduce assets (disinvestment).

• Capital expenditure (Option 4): Spending that creates assets or repays loan principal, not interest.

question: Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Limited established as a fully owned subsidiary of the Reserve bank in the year _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1995.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Private Limited (BRBNMPL) (भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक नोट मुद्रण लिमिटेड) was established in 1995 as a fully owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

• It was set up to augment the production of bank notes in India and bridge the gap between demand and supply of currency notes.

• It operates currency note printing presses at Mysuru (Karnataka) and Salboni (West Bengal).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The RBI is the sole authority to issue currency notes in India (except the one-rupee note, issued by the Government of India).

• BRBNMPL is registered under the Companies Act.

• India also has government-owned presses under Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India Ltd (SPMCIL).

NOTE

• 1994 (Option 1): Incorrect year of establishment.

• 1996 (Option 2): Incorrect; BRBNMPL was set up in 1995.

• 1997 (Option 3): Incorrect year of establishment.

question: In which year was the fixed rate repos in government securities was introduced to give maneuverability in liquidity management?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1997.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fixed rate repos (निश्चित दर रेपो) in government securities were introduced in 1997 to give the RBI greater manoeuvrability in liquidity management.

• Repo (Repurchase) operations allow the RBI to inject or absorb liquidity in the banking system.

• This paved the way for using the repo as a key monetary policy instrument.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) was later introduced in 2000 based on the Narasimham Committee (II) recommendations.

• Under repo, banks borrow from the RBI against government securities.

• The repo rate is a major tool to control inflation and money supply.

NOTE

• 1995 (Option 1): Incorrect; fixed rate repos were introduced in 1997.

• 1998 (Option 3): Incorrect year for this introduction.

• 1996 (Option 4): Incorrect year for this introduction.

question: The Clearing Corporation of India Limited (CCIL) was established in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2001.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Clearing Corporation of India Limited (CCIL) (क्लियरिंग कॉरपोरेशन ऑफ इंडिया लिमिटेड) was established in 2001.

• It was set up to provide guaranteed clearing and settlement functions for transactions in money markets, government securities and foreign exchange.

• It acts as a central counterparty (CCP) for these market segments.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• CCIL began operations in the government securities market in 2002.

• It reduces settlement risk and improves efficiency in Indian financial markets.

• It is regulated by the Reserve Bank of India.

NOTE

• 2004 (Option 1): Incorrect year of establishment.

• 2006 (Option 2): Incorrect; CCIL was established in 2001.

• 2005 (Option 3): Incorrect year of establishment.

question: As per census 2001, what was the sex ratio of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 933.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census 2001, the sex ratio of India (लिंगानुपात) was 933 females per 1000 males.

• Sex ratio is defined as the number of females per 1000 males in a population.

• It improved to 943 in the Census 2011.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kerala has consistently recorded the highest sex ratio among states.

• Haryana recorded one of the lowest sex ratios.

• The Census in India is conducted every 10 years; 1872 saw the first census and 1881 the first synchronous one.

NOTE

• 912 (Option 2): Not the 2001 all-India sex ratio.

• 920 (Option 3): Not the 2001 all-India sex ratio (this is closer to 1911 levels).

• 981 (Option 4): Much higher than the actual 2001 figure of 933.

question: In the context of economy, if _____ is deducted from the gross value added to obtain the Net value added obtained.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Depreciation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Net Value Added (NVA) = Gross Value Added (GVA) − Depreciation (मूल्यह्रास).

• Depreciation (consumption of fixed capital) is the fall in the value of fixed assets due to wear and tear, use and obsolescence.

• Deducting depreciation converts a 'gross' measure into a 'net' measure.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Similarly, Net National Product (NNP) = Gross National Product (GNP) − Depreciation.

• Gross measures include depreciation; net measures exclude it.

• Net indirect tax (Indirect taxes − Subsidies) is used to move between 'market price' and 'factor cost' valuations.

NOTE

• Net indirect tax (Option 2): Deducted to convert market price value to factor cost value, not gross to net.

• Subsidy (Option 3): Added back (or netted with indirect taxes) in factor-cost conversions, not for gross-to-net.

• Wage (Option 4): A component of income/cost, not deducted to get net value added.

question: Where did Siddhartha Gautam meditate for many days?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bodh Gaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Siddhartha Gautam meditated for many days under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya (बोधगया) in present-day Bihar, where he attained enlightenment (Nirvana/Bodhi).

• After enlightenment he came to be known as the Buddha ('the enlightened one').

• Bodh Gaya is the most sacred pilgrimage site for Buddhists.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Lumbini (Nepal) is his birthplace; Sarnath (near Varanasi) is where he gave his first sermon; Kushinagar is where he attained Mahaparinirvana.

• The Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• His first sermon at Sarnath is called Dharma Chakra Pravartana.

NOTE

• Lumbini (Option 1): The birthplace of Siddhartha Gautam, not the place of enlightenment.

• Varanasi (Option 3): Near Sarnath where he delivered his first sermon, not where he attained enlightenment.

• Ujjain (Option 4): An ancient city associated with Emperor Ashoka and Vikramaditya, not the Buddha's enlightenment.

question: On the banks of which river was the Harappan site of 'Harappa' discovered in 1920-22?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ravi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Harappan site of Harappa was discovered on the banks of the River Ravi (रावी) in 1920–22.

• It is located in the Montgomery (Sahiwal) district of Punjab in present-day Pakistan.

• It was excavated under the guidance of Daya Ram Sahni.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Harappa gives its name to the Harappan (Indus Valley) Civilisation.

• Mohenjo-daro, another major site, lies on the banks of the Indus river and was discovered in 1922 by R. D. Banerji.

• The Indus Valley Civilisation was a Bronze Age urban civilisation.

NOTE

• Ganga (Option 2): A major north Indian river, but Harappa is not on its banks.

• Luni (Option 3): An inland river of Rajasthan draining into the Rann of Kutch; not linked to Harappa.

• Yamuna (Option 4): A tributary of the Ganga; Harappa does not lie on it.
